prompt_text:
Write a song using music theory principles and rich instrument captions, without relying on drums, electric guitars, or bass. The song is a eurobeat song. Use the following format: [Verse 1: Lyrics], [Verse 1: Rich Instrument Caption]. Keep in mind the principles of music theory as you craft your song.

Example of rich captions
The main soundtrack of an arcade game. It is fast-paced and retro, with a catchy guitar riff. The music is repetitive and easy to remember, but with unexpected sounds, like cymbal crashes or drum rolls.	
A rising synth is playing an arpeggio with a lot of reverb. It is backed by pads, sub bass line and soft drums. This song is full of synth sounds creating a soothing and adventurous atmosphere. It may be playing at a festival during two songs for a buildup.
raw_response:
[Verse 1: Lyrics]
The neon clock strikes midnight on the boulevard of dreams
A velvet hush descends where the silver moonlight beams
No thunder in the chest, no roar of steel and wire
Just violins igniting a slow-burning fire
The melody takes flight on a current made of air
A heartbeat made of silence, a rhythm rare and bare

[Verse 1: Rich Instrument Caption]
A solo Concert Grand Piano opens with a staccato sixteenth-note ostinato in A-flat major, outlining a I-vi-ii-V7 progression (Ab - Fm7 - Bbm7 - Eb7) with aggressive, percussive attack simulating a 150 BPM sequencer drive. First Violins enter *sul tasto* on the downbeat of measure two, sustaining a high Eb (the V/IV) before cascading down a Lydian-mode run (Eb-F-G-A-Bb) to resolve on the major 7th of the tonic. A French Horn section punctuates the off-beats (the "and" of 2 and 4) with tight, stopped-horn stabs, mimicking the Eurobeat "off-beat bass" syncopation through timbral weight rather than low frequency. A Harpsichord doubles the piano's right hand an octave higher, adding brittle, plucked transients to define the rhythmic grid without a kick drum.

[Pre-Chorus: Lyrics]
The tempo starts to climb, a staircase made of sound
Circle of fifths turning, spinning round and round
Secondary dominants pull the tonic near
Deceptive cadence—wait, the drop is here
Suspension in the violas, tension in the air
Resolution delayed until the moment's there

[Pre-Chorus: Rich Instrument Caption]
The harmonic rhythm accelerates to two chords per bar. The Piano shifts to block chords voiced in fourths (quartal harmony) ascending chromatically: Bbm7 - E7 (V/vi) - Abmaj7 - D7 (V/ii) - Gbmaj7 - C7 (V/vi) - Fm7 - Bb7 (V/IV). A full String section (Violins I/II, Violas, Cellos) executes a measured tremolo *sul ponticello*, swelling *crescendo* from *pianissimo* to *fortissimo* over eight bars, their combined overtones creating a dense, white-noise-like spectral energy replacing white-noise snare risers. A Solo Cello plays a relentless pedal point on Ab (tonic) in the low register, bowing *detaché* sixteenth notes to anchor the tonal center and provide the "driving" motor rhythm. A Glockenspiel strikes a repeating high Eb (dominant pedal) on every downbeat, a piercing metronome of pure sine-wave clarity.

[Chorus: Lyrics]
This is Eurobeat, stripped down to the bone
Where counterpoint and harmony sit on the throne
The melody screams loud on a trumpet's golden cry
No amplifier needed, just the reason why
Parallel fifths forbidden, voice leading is the law
We ride the wave of theory, we ride the perfect flaw
Feel the sub-bass in the cello's deepest groan
This is the sound of the silent zone

[Chorus: Rich Instrument Caption]
Full orchestral *tutti* at *fortississimo*. The Main Melody is carried by a Solo Trumpet *con sordino* (harmon mute), playing a soaring, syncopated line in the upper register (written C6-G6) utilizing the "Eurobeat third" (major 3rd bent slightly sharp for brightness). The Harmony is realized by a 4-part Saxophone Quartet (Soprano, Alto, Tenor

reasoning_text:
The user wants a Eurobeat song written without drums, electric guitars, or bass.
This is a significant constraint because Eurobeat is *defined* by its driving 4-on-the-floor kick, heavy synth bass, and energetic guitars.
I need to simulate the *energy*, *harmony*, *melody*, and *rhythm* of Eurobeat using only permitted instruments (likely orchestral, acoustic, piano, synths that aren't "bass" per se, brass, strings, woodwinds, percussion that isn't a "drum kit" - though the prompt says "without relying on drums", so I should avoid standard drum kit sounds. I can use orchestral percussion, hand percussion, body percussion, or melodic rhythm).
The format requires: [Verse 1: Lyrics], [Verse 1: Rich Instrument Caption].
I need to apply music theory principles (circle of fifths, secondary dominants, deceptive cadences, modal interchange, typical Eurobeat chord progressions like vi-IV-V-I or I-V-vi-IV but spiced up).
